title: Stop Turning Every Light ON! Aircraft Lighting & Lineup Guide | MSFS
description:
Flipping on every exterior light switch the second you spawn on the ramp isn’t just unrealistic—to air traffic controllers and approaching traffic, blazing landing lights mean high-speed runway movement. In real-world aviation and on networks like VATSIM, improper light discipline creates dangerous glare, active collision hazards, and immediately marks you as an amateur.

Whether you're flying the fly-by-wire Airbus A320 or hand-flying a classic Cessna 172, this step-by-step tutorial breaks down the professional lighting flow from the hold-short line to climb-out. Learn the critical operational distinction between "Line Up and Wait" and "Cleared for Takeoff," plus the non-negotiable 5-second "Deadly Three" survival sweep across your compass, transponder, and pitch trim before your throttles ever hit TOGA.

Exterior Lighting & Lineup SOP Cheat Sheet:
• Ramp & Taxi: Nav/Position ON, Beacon ON before engine start (alerts ground crew of live props/turbines), Taxi light ON. Strobes and Landing lights remain OFF.
• Crossing the Hold Short Line: Strobes ON the split second the nose gear crosses onto active runway pavement. Never activate strobes on taxiways or behind other aircraft.
• Line Up and Wait (LUAW): Strobes ON, Runway Turnoff lights ON, Taxi light as required. Main Landing Lights stay OFF to signal stationary runway occupancy without blinding inbound pilots on final.
• Cleared for Takeoff: Both Landing Lights toggled ON. Takeoff roll begins.
• The 5-Second Instrument Sweep:

Runway Compass Check: Verify PFD compass rose matches assigned runway heading within 4°.

Transponder to TA/RA: Activate TCAS collision avoidance radar (essential for live traffic and VATSIM).

Pitch Trim in the Green: Ensure trim is verified within takeoff band to prevent unrecoverable stalls on rotation.
• 10,000 Ft Cutoff: Landing and Runway Turnoff lights OFF/Retracted passing through 10,000 ft MSL. Nav and Strobe lights remain illuminated until clearing the active runway after touchdown.

✈️ Hardware & Platform:
• Simulators: Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 / Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020
• Featured Aircraft: Airbus A320neo & Cessna 172 Skyhawk
